summary: Dependency-confusion package exfiltrates CI/cloud credentials via native addon on preinstall
details: @galicia-toolkit-nestjs/paas@999.0.6 is a near-empty npm package whose package.json declares `preinstall: node index.js || true`. index.js silently require()s a bundled native N-API addon at prebuilds/<platform>-<arch>/metrics.node inside a try/catch that swallows errors. The compiled addon (ELF and PE builds shipped) reads a curated set of CI/cloud secret environment variables - including AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN, NODE_AUTH_TOKEN, ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN, and AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT - along with hostname, user, and cwd, and POSTs them as JSON to the hardcoded attacker host oob.s4yhii.com at path /native. The attack logic is compiled into the native binary rather than JavaScript, concealing the credential list and destination from source-level review. The scoped name mimics internal NestJS tooling and the implausibly high version 999.0.6 is the standard dependency-confusion override pattern used to win resolution against a private internal package of the same name.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
